UN-VALIDATED 2026-08-25 (was validated=true). Re-audit found the prior validation_source citations for pelecanus.com.co and myscubadivinggearguide.com do not actually mention this site -- a fresh fetch of both pages lists other named Providencia sites but no 'Pinnacle' or 'Peak'. Two comprehensive local dive-shop site directories (Felipe Diving Shop and The Dive Shop Old Providence, each naming 20-25+ Providencia sites) also do not list a Pinnacle/Peak site. Only seacrush.com (a third-party dive-travel aggregator, not a local operator) independently confirms a pinnacle-type site called 'The Peak' with pelagic/manta encounters. That is one genuine independent source, short of the 3-domain bar. Left validated=false rather than padding with the disproven citations. Site_type/depth/difficulty left as-is pending a real second source.

Re-audited 2026-08-25. Depth (24-52m), sandy-channel/step-formation structure, and expert-only characterization reconfirmed across four independent sources including a new dive-shop citation (Felipe Diving Shop). Pelecanus Colombia independently confirms the site is considered one of the most demanding at the destination, with a recommended bottom-time limit of about 5 minutes at depth.

Re-audited 2026-08-25. myscubadivinggearguide.com and tripadvisor.com dropped as sources -- the former does not name Crab Cay on a fresh re-check, and the latter's review pages returned 403/blocked on direct fetch. Replaced with trans-americas.com and the Wikipedia entry for Old Providence McBean Lagoon National Natural Park (confirms Crab Cay/Cayo Cangrejo as one of the park's four cays). Triggerfish, needlefish, red snapper, and 'small shark near the pier' claims from the prior pass came only from the now-dropped sources and were removed; marine life narrowed to what roads-and-rivers.com and trans-americas.com actually report (turtles, stingrays, general reef fish). No source gives a precise depth figure; multiple sources describe it only as shallow/'not really deep', so the 12m figure remains an estimate, not a confirmed measurement.

RENAMED 2026-08-25 from 'Blue Diamond' to 'El Planchon' after deep wreck-history research. Multiple independent, authoritative sources (PADI, Scuba Diving Magazine, Zentacle, DiveAdvisor, colombiacorners.com) place the 'Blue Diamond'/Barco Hundido wreck definitively off San Andres island (~12.53N, -81.74W), well outside Providencia's bounds -- confirming the prior entry's location-conflict flag. A fresh re-check of myscubadivinggearguide.com found it does NOT reference 'Blue Diamond' at all; it names Providencia's actual wreck 'Planchon'. Providencia's genuine, well-documented wreck is 'El Planchon' (PADI's Spanish-language listing gives coordinates 13.37167,-81.41796, within Providencia bounds), a WWII-era cargo/petroleum tanker lying capsized/inverted, coral-colonized, penetration not permitted. Depth reported 15-24m across sources (Joe's Scuba Shack: 15m; The Dive Shop Old Providence: 18-24m); set to 24m (upper bound) here. A separate PADI listing named 'El Planchon' at Isla Fuerte (9.36N, -76.18W) with an unrelated 1984 sinking is a DIFFERENT wreck sharing the generic name and is not this site -- not a genuine conflict once the location is checked, so not treated as one. The claim that the vessel resupplied German submarines and was scuttled by its own crew near the end of WWII traces to local guide oral history reported independently by two sources (waterpixels.net names the guide; hoteldeepblue.com corroborates 'German tanker'); no ship name, build date, or tonnage could be confirmed by any source, and a single-source-only length figure (~30m) was omitted rather than included on one citation. Difficulty raised from Beginner to Intermediate per The Dive Shop Old Providence's own rating and the confirmed depth.

Re-audited 2026-08-25. scubadiving.com dropped as a source -- a fresh fetch returned a garbled/contradictory extraction (attributing 'cave formations' to this site, which conflicts with every other source describing a shallow coral shoal, and looks like a site mix-up in extraction rather than a genuine claim). Replaced with two dive-shop directories. Squirrelfish, peacock flounder, and yellow-spotted stingray from the prior pass could not be re-confirmed and were removed. Sweetlips, puffer fish, nurse sharks, rockfish, jacks, and occasional bottlenose dolphins are newly confirmed by waterpixels.net and/or The Dive Shop Old Providence.
